full.description: This is a microscopic blood smear showing red blood cells stained with Wright's stain. Within one of the erythrocytes, a ring-form trophozoite is clearly visible as a delicate ring with a chromatin dot. The appearance is characteristic of an intracellular parasite infection within the blood. The most likely diagnosis is malaria caused by Plasmodium vivax.

blind.description: This image is a blood smear micrograph viewed under oil immersion with Wright's stain. The sample shows elements of hematologic tissue. Parasites characteristic of malaria, specifically Plasmodium vivax trophozoites and ring forms, are visible within or associated with the blood cells. The most likely diagnosis is malaria caused by Plasmodium vivax infection.
